recipes.name: Caribbean Jerk Stir-Fry
ingredients_raw: 1 green bell pepper, seeded and cubed
1 red bell pepper, seeded and cubed
0.75 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into strips

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir bell pepper and onion in hot oil until slightly tender, 5 to 7 minutes; transfer onto a plate and set aside.
Add chicken to the same skillet and season with jerk seasoning; cook and stir until chicken is cooked through and no longer pink inside.

Return bell peppers and onions to the skillet and pour in plum sauce; toss to combine. Cook until peppers and onions are heated through, 3 to 5 minutes. Sprinkle with soy sauce and chopped peanuts to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Caribbean Jerk Stir-Fry
raw_recipe.description: This chicken stir-fry recipe with plum sauce gets a fiery Caribbean twist with the addition of jerk seasoning for a sweet and spicy dish. Delicious!

review.reviewBody: I wasn't sure how the Caribbean/Asian blend of spices would work. TERRIFIC!! I was pleasantly surprised. I followed this recipe with only a few modifications. I doubled the receipe and cooked 2lbs. of boneless skinless chicken breasts in olive oil with the jerk seasoning. I used frozen stir fry vegetables to save time (2 packages). I also doubled the sauce with 2 jars of Asian plum sauce. Served with brown rice. Absolutely delicious! Will defintely make again, next time I will try with fresh vegetables. My son even ate two servings!

I followed the recipe as is. It turn out very good. I used a different Jerk sauce. 1/2 cup of sesame oil and 1/4 cup of molasses and 2tbs soy sauce, 11/2 tablespoons ground allspice, 4to 6 cloves garlic, 1 to 2 habaneros pepper, 1 bunch of scallions or 1 onions cut up, 1 bunch of fresh thyme or ground, black pepper. combine all ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth. pour into a saucepan and cook over medium heat until the sauce change color about 10 to 15 minute, and then pour over the chicken and vegetables. This is very good and spicy. lot of heat!!! I had it with jasmine rice.

This is a great recipe. My wife is Jamaican and I wasnt sure how the jerk would work with the sweet for them but her family loves it. I made a few slight additions by frying and cutting up a few strips of bacon and adding water chestnuts at the end. I have found that the flavor is excellent when you use Bonne Maman plum preserves with the recipe.

It was amazing! Such great sweet heat. I didn't have plum sauce so I used sweet chili sauce and added a tablespoon of honey. Tossed in fresh broccoli at the end before adding peppers and onions back in. Left out peanuts (allergy). My husband loved it. My kids thought it was a bit spicy but still ate it all. Will definitely make again.
Unusual flavor combination but very tasty and easy! I suggest marinading the chicken overnight in jerk spices, lemon/lime juice, and soy sauce for extra depth of flavor. Thanks for the recipe!

Fantastic recipe! A real crowd pleaser among a very picky family of nine. The only things I changed, was omitting the peanuts, and instead of sprinkling the jerk spice on top of the chicken and mixing it in, I rubbed each individual piece of chicken with the jerk seasoning and let it sit in the fridge for about twenty minutes before cooking- definitely gives it more kick this way.

Excellent flavor!....couldn’t find plum sauce so used Hoisin instead and it was a great substitute. Might add additional veggies next time such as pea pods or water chestnuts, and will definitely triple the recipe so there are leftovers to be had the next day. Five stars on the YUM meter!

This was great! I used a small onion and fresh garlic, and then added broccoli, carrots and zucchini, and more of the jack seasoning on the chicken. Only used one large red pepper, since I had so many other veges and don't particularly care for green peppers. Served over wild rice. Delicious. I just wish plum sauce didn't have so much sugar in it. I'll try using half the called-for plum sauce next time. But it's definitely a solid dish.

This is my daughter's favorite recipe. She demands I make it every week. Changes I made:

- I don't have plum sauce so I use apple juice 

- Add shaved/sticks of carrots to peppers

- Add scrambled eggs at the end 

- Add spicy pepper (jalapeno, poblano, etc.) to chicken

- Served over jasmine rice
Very good. Couldn't find plum sauce so used watered down apricot preserves, works great. Added more jerk seasoning once everything was mixed and some salt. Delicious!
Delicious. Tasty with just the right amount of heat. We added a small can of water chestnuts and some chopped garlic to the mix just for fun. Awesome.
Perfect as-is.
Good dish but could be a bit more spicy
Everyone in my house LOVED this!

Writing my first review on this App, after trying, at least 100 different recipes... This was, simply put, AMAZING!!!! Excellent mix of flavors and sweet/spicy contrast!!! We doubled the amount of chicken, so we also doubled the amount of jerk seasoning and plum sauce. If you’re on the fence about trying this one, get off the fence bro!! DO IT!!!
I'm not a big fan of the texture of peanuts in my food, so I used 1.5 tsp of peanut butter
Who knew plum sauce would be such a game-changer?
We doubled the chicken & added brocolli. Going to make it again this week!
It was a good recipe for my first stir fry!
Really nice flavours. We always use Baron jerk seasoning.
